checks.scope: Literal dollar characters in rendered prose are the intended subject.
checks.observable: Classify prose versus code and distinguish a literal character from intended math markup.
checks.consistency: AP-63 places protocol variable syntax in code spans, avoiding accidental escaping.
checks.exceptions: Code spans and fences are explicitly protected from escaping that corrupts code.
checks.fix: Escape a literal prose dollar while retaining code bytes.
checks.expression: Read the literal qualifier across the entry; no new verdict about the current renderer was inferred.

rationale: The literal-versus-code rule is inspectable. This review does not independently validate the source's renderer-specific GFM claim.

checks.scope: Evaluated symbol ids are separated from technique/resource/rule names.
checks.observable: Inspect the declared symbol class and its spelling.
checks.consistency: DP-19 supplies the same naming stance; input/output identity is permitted for a real shared value.
checks.exceptions: External tool parameter spellings and kebab-case name identities are explicitly retained.
checks.fix: Rename symbol ids while preserving exact external parameter mirrors.
checks.expression: The two identifier classes and their exceptions make the rule deterministic.

rationale: snake_case for values and kebab-case for named definitions are distinct conventions; an external cloudId parameter mirror is not an invented local symbol spelling.

checks.scope: A caveat on one instruction is distinguished from the instruction itself.
checks.observable: The parser's treatment of indentation provides a concrete consequence to verify.
checks.consistency: The any-indent conditional-ladder exception is broader than DP-31's note requirement.
checks.exceptions: Primary ordered work should be exempt; fallback ladders qualifying one instruction need a narrower exception.
checks.fix: Move local branches into notes; keep whole-step/activity selection in structure.
checks.expression: Replace 'at any indent' with a semantic distinction between work and qualifying caveat.

rationale: The note rule has a clear purpose, but its ladder exception can admit the very flattened branches it detects.

checks.scope: A local rule applying to only one Protocol block is well scoped.
checks.observable: Trace the predicate to the single instruction/block it qualifies.
checks.consistency: The same trigger and note/prose repair are already in AP-25.
checks.exceptions: Cross-cutting rules and existing local notes are appropriately excluded.
checks.fix: Demotion to the qualifying instruction retains the actual constraint.
checks.expression: The cross-reference to AP-25 does not establish a disjoint boundary.

rationale: Consolidate this duplicate local-scope criterion while leaving AP-59 to own note syntax.

checks.scope: Repeated literals and hard-coded uses of an already declared path are the subjects.
checks.observable: Match semantic path identity and inspect existing input/default/local definitions.
checks.consistency: Fits AP-127's declared-value use and AP-55's shared contract placement.
checks.exceptions: Single-use values, the canonical definition, and similar-looking distinct paths are expressly excluded.
checks.fix: Factor one semantic location and correct wrong-location uses without inventing a shadow variable.
checks.expression: The semantic-identity exception prevents mechanical string deduplication of unrelated paths.

rationale: Repeated references to the same artifact root can share a designator; two coincidentally similar paths with different roles need not.

checks.scope: Local binding sites, local reads, and declared/ambient inputs are distinguished.
checks.observable: The bind/read spellings and textual producer position can be inspected; path reachability is a separate check.
checks.consistency: Its ambient-input exemption needs the same effective-contract model as AP-16.
checks.exceptions: Mutually exclusive producers and declared inputs are expressly permitted.
checks.fix: Bind a real local once at its producer, read its name, or remove a dead binding.
checks.expression: Name the source of ambient inputs rather than implying an open set from examples.

rationale: The local-use criterion is clear; align the ambient exception with declared-input quality checks. Textual order alone is not a claim of path-total production.

checks.scope: Code tokens are separated from descriptive prose and navigable link targets.
checks.observable: Inspect Markdown spans/fences and the declared token class.
checks.consistency: Braces remain required by AP-52; invocation argument names use AP-56's different form.
checks.exceptions: Already protected code, ordinary nouns, links, and parameter labels are explicit exceptions.
checks.fix: Wrap the full token/command in one span and preserve its actual code content.
checks.expression: Fragmented spans and escaped local markers receive specific unambiguous repairs.

rationale: Formatting a whole command as one code span preserves both readability and its embedded designators.

checks.scope: Boolean value identifiers are the subject, not arbitrary state or enum names.
checks.observable: Compare the identifier with the proposition for which the Boolean is true.
checks.consistency: Implements DP-19's affirmative predicate stance without forcing one prefix.
checks.exceptions: Clear unprefixed predicates and meaningful is/has/can/should forms are retained.
checks.fix: Rename to a predicate that preserves the actual truth condition.
checks.expression: The true-value meaning, not a token-count rule, determines whether the stem is affirmative.

rationale: A generic status_flag conceals the true condition; ready or has_findings identifies it. Any rename must preserve that condition across consumers.
